title: Career roadmap · Mobility Policy Advisor
summary: Build from transport and urban-systems research into evidence-based mobility policy, combining travel behaviour, spatial analysis, public transport, infrastructure, regulation, climate goals and data-driven decision-making.

facts.Timeline assumption: The roadmap assumes a 2026-start Ph.D. pathway. Early work develops transport and urban analytics; the middle phase builds policy evaluation and stakeholder capability; later work moves toward city, state, national or international mobility strategy.

horizons.question: What can I enter now?
horizons.output: Build expertise in transport planning, urban economics, GIS, travel behaviour, mobility data, public transport and policy evaluation.

horizons.question: How should I specialise?
horizons.output: Become a subject-matter specialist in public transport, sustainable mobility, road safety, shared mobility, active transport or transport decarbonisation.

horizons.question: How should I evolve?
horizons.output: Lead cross-agency mobility studies and translate evidence into investment, regulatory and urban-development decisions.

horizons.question: How can I remain relevant?
horizons.output: Advise governments and institutions on integrated mobility systems using AI, real-time data, climate analysis, accessibility and long-term urban scenarios.

rows.text: Transport planning, urban systems and policy fundamentals

Produce a transparent policy appraisal comparing at least two interventions
Create a road-safety or mode-shift intervention assessment with measurable indicators
Build a scenario model showing how a defined policy changes mobility outcomes
Produce a policy brief with stakeholder map, implementation responsibilities and risks
Deliver a publication-quality policy study with recommendations, evidence and implementation roadmap

blocks.text: Mobility policy is increasingly a systems problem rather than a road-building problem. Career progression

Ph.D. Researcher → Mobility/Transport Researcher → Senior Mobility Policy Analyst → Mobility Policy Lead → Principal Transport Policy Advisor → Mobility Strategy Director → National/Regional Mobility Policy Advisor → Chief Mobility/Transport Strategy Advisor

items: 15+ years, with government and consulting career structures differing substantially
blocks.label: Typical planning ranges are

blocks.text: Ph.D. routes

A senior mobility policy advisor should be able to connect transport infrastructure with land use, housing, economic development, climate, public health and accessibility. The strongest profile will combine quantitative evidence with an understanding of institutions and implementation. AI and real-time mobility data should become decision-support tools, not substitutes for public consultation, governance or policy judgment.
